svg.title: Anatomy of an X.509 v3 server certificate
svg.desc: A table of the fields in the certificate for api.example.com. Version: v3. Serial number: unique per issuing CA. Signature algorithm: for example ecdsa-with-SHA256. Issuer: CN=Example TLS CA R1. Validity: notBefore and notAfter, 90 days apart, checked by clients. Subject: CN=api.example.com, which modern clients ignore for hostname checks. Subject public key: for example an ECDSA P-256 key, whose private half stays on the server. Subject alternative name: DNS:api.example.com and DNS:app.example.com, which clients match against the hostname. Key usage and extended key usage: digitalSignature and serverAuth. Basic constraints: CA false, so it cannot sign other certificates. Authority information access: the URL of the issuer certificate. CRL distribution points: where revocation lists are published. Signed certificate timestamps: proof that the certificate was logged in Certificate Transparency logs. Signature: the issuer's signature over all fields above.

g.text: Certificate for api.example.com: fields and what they are for
unique per issuing CA; used to identify the certificate in revocation lists
for example ecdsa-with-SHA256: how the issuer signed
CN=Example TLS CA R1: who signed it; must match the next certificate up
notBefore / notAfter, 90 days apart: checked by every client
CN=api.example.com: legacy; modern clients ignore it for hostname checks
for example an ECDSA P-256 key; the private half never leaves the server
DNS:api.example.com, DNS:app.example.com: matched against the hostname
digitalSignature / serverAuth: allowed to authenticate TLS servers
URL of the issuer's certificate, for clients that need to fetch it
where the CA publishes revoked serial numbers
signed certificate timestamps: proof it was logged in Certificate Transparency
the issuer's signature over all fields above
Clients match the hostname to the SAN and check dates, usage, and the issuer's signature.
